title: Strings check
instructions: Five questions on indexing, slicing and immutability.

questions.explanation: A slice starts at index 1 and stops before index 4, so it takes the characters at 1, 2 and 3: y, t, h.
A negative index counts from the end, so -1 is the last character.
The space is a character too, so the string has three characters.
Multiplying text by a whole number repeats it.

questions.prompt: After word = 'cat', what happens when Python runs word[0] = 'b'?
options: A TypeError, because strings cannot be changed
questions.explanation: Strings are immutable. To get 'bat' you build a new string, for example 'b' + word[1:].

title: Initials
instructions:
`name` is set to `"Ada Lovelace"`. Using **indexing and slicing** (do not type the answers), create:

- `first`: the first name, `Ada`
- `last`: the last name, `Lovelace`
- `initials`: the first letter of each name, `AL`

Then print `initials`.
